question.:question/problem:
Consider the matrix $A$ below. Which set of entries should be replaced by $0$ to obtain row echelon form **using the fewest replacements**? Leave all other entries unchanged.

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 4 & 7 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The minimum set is $a_{21}$ and $a_{43}$. Replace these 2 entries with $0$:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 4 & 7 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}\,\longrightarrow\,\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 4 & 7 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{bmatrix}
$$

The nonzero rows have leading entries in columns 1, 2, 3, 4, in strictly increasing order, and all zero rows are at the bottom. 

Restoring $a_{21}$ would put the leading entry of row 2 in column 1, which is not to the right of the leading entry in row 1. Restoring $a_{43}$ would put the leading entry of row 4 in column 3, which is not to the right of the leading entry in row 3. No set with fewer than 2 replacements satisfies both the leading-entry order and zero-row conditions.

Entries to the right of a leading entry may remain nonzero.
